references.text: Cleopas is possibly the husband of Mary, who was one of the women at the cross. In [ref:Joh 19:25|John 19:25], "Mary the wife of Clopas" is mentioned, and many scholars identify this Clopas with Cleopas from the road to Emmaus.
The context for Cleopas' answer: In [ref:Luk 24:13-17|Luke 24:13-17], two disciples are on their way to Emmaus, discussing what has happened, without recognizing the risen Jesus who joins them.

The expression "Σὺ μόνος παροικεῖς Ἰερουσαλήμ" (are you the only one living in Jerusalem and do not know?) reflects the idea that the events in Jerusalem were widely known. In [ref:Luk 2:44|Luke 2:44], we see a similar motif where something is so well-known that ignorance of it seems unthinkable.
In [ref:Luk 24:19-24|Luke 24:19-24], Cleopas and his companion elaborate on what "what has happened" in Jerusalem was about: Jesus' crucifixion, death, and the first reports of the empty tomb.

The idea that the events surrounding Jesus were widely known in Jerusalem has a parallel in [ref:Apg 26:26|Acts 26:26], where Paul says to King Agrippa that these things have not been done in a corner, but are well-known.

In [ref:Apg 2:22-23|Acts 2:22-23], Peter emphasizes in his Pentecost sermon that Jesus of Nazareth and his deeds were well-known to all in Jerusalem, which aligns with Cleopas' surprise that anyone should not know what had happened.
